questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Why do we have to accept these conditions?

options.text: Why do these conditions have to be accepted?
Why should these conditions be accepted?
These conditions do not have to be accepted.
Why are these conditions needed to be accepted?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• In the given active sentence, 'these conditions' is the object.
 
• The passive form of the sentence follows the structure:
 
 
• **Why + be + subject + past participle + Object ( not mandatory ) + ?**
 
 

Hence, the correct passive form is: ***Why do these conditions have to be accepted?***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] ***Additional Information__***

 
• Option 2 =** Incorrect** = It doesn't follow the proper structure of interrogative passive voice. 
 
• Option 3 = **Incorrec**t = It doesn't follow the proper structure of interrogative passive voice. 
 
• Option 4 =** Incorrect** = It doesn't follow the proper structure of interrogative passive voice.

questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

It is said that Einstein was a genius.

options.text: People are saying that Einstein was a genius.
People have said that Einstein was a genius.
People say that Einstein was a genius.
People said that Einstein was a genius.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passive sentence **"It is said that Einstein was a genius**" can be converted into the active voice using the subject "**People**".
 
• As there is** no particular object **mentioned in the sentence since "**that Einstein was a genius"** is **a phrase**. So it is categorized as** 'without object in passive voice. '**
 
• The phrase **"It is said that"** translates into the active form as **"People say that".**
 
• The tense of the verb should remain** consistent** with the original sentence. Here,** "say"** is in the simple present tense, matching the original sentence's implied meaning.
 
• Format of active voice :** Subject + Main verb ( simple present tense here ) + Object**

Hence, the correct active form is '***People say that Einstein was a genius*.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Active voice emphasizes the subject performing the action, making the sentence **cleare**r and more **direct.**
 
• In passive voice, the focus is on the action and the** recipient**, which can sometimes lead to** ambiguity or less dynamic sentences.**

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Why didn’t your father accompany you?

options.text: Why didn’t you be accompanied by your father?
Why were you not accompanied by your father?
Why wasn’t your father accompanied by you?
Why have you not been accompanied by your father?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In passive voice sentences, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The tense and the question form are maintained while changing the voice from active to passive.
 
• The subject of the active sentence "**your father"** becomes the agent in the passive sentence, and **"you**" becomes the new subject.
 
• The correct structure for the passive form of a past simple question is 
 
 
• **"Why + was/were + subject + verb (past participle)?**"
 
 

Hence, the correct Passive voice is :** *Why were you not accompanied by your father?***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The use of passive voice can shift the focus of the sentence from the doer of the action to the action itself or the recipient of the action.
 
• This can be useful for emphasizing the action or for situations where the doer is unknown or less important.

questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

A party is being given by her on the occasion of her sixteenth birthday.

options.text: She will give a party on the occasion of her sixteenth birthday.
She is giving a party on the occasion of her sixteenth birthday.
She was giving a party on the occasion of her sixteenth birthday.
She has given a party on the occasion of her sixteenth birthday.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the **passive voice** and needs to be converted to the **active voice.**
 
• In the **passive voice,** the subject of the sentence (in this case **'her'**) **is the recipient of the action.**
 
• In the** active voice**, the subject of the sentence (in this case** 'She**')** performs **the** action.**
 
• The correct active form of the sentence should be in** the present continuous tense to match the passive construction 'is being given'.**
 
• Format = **Subject (she) + Verb (present continuous tense here) + Object (a party) + prepositional phrase (on the occasion of her sixteenth birthday.)**

Therefore, the correct active form is: '**She is giving a party on the occasion of her sixteenth birthday'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__** Other options are invalid due to incorrect tense used there.

 
• Option 1 = **Incorrect,** the tense used here is in future indefinite tense. It doesn't match with the tense given in the question.
 
• Option 2 =** Incorrect**, the tense used here is in past continuous tense. It doesn't match with the tense given in the question.
 
• Option 3 =** Incorrect**, the tense used here is in present perfect tense. It doesn't match with the tense given in the question.

questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

The workers will not be satisfied with empty promises.

options.text: Empty promises cannot satisfy the workers.
Empty promises do not satisfy the workers.
Empty promises will not satisfy the workers.
Empty promises would not satisfy the workers.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence is in the **future tense** and uses the modal verb '**will'.**
 
• When converting from passive to active voice, the subject and object of the sentence are swapped.
 
• The sentence in the active voice will follow the structure: **Subject + will + base verb + object**.
 
• In the given sentence, "**The workers**" is the object, and "**empty promises" **is the subject in the active voice.

Therefore, the correct active form is: **"Empty promises will not satisfy the workers."**

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Everybody wants others to respect them.

options.text: Everybody wanted to be respected by others.
Everybody wants to be respected by others.
They want others to be respected by everybody.
Everybody wants to respect others.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sentence, the active voice is changed to the passive voice.
 
• The object of the **active voice **(others) becomes the subject in the** passive voice.**
 
• The verb form changes to include the appropriate form of '**to be'** (here, '**to be respected**'). As it is an infinitive statement.
 
• The subject of the active voice (Everybody) becomes the object in the passive voice.
 
• Hence, the transformation is done correctly in option 2.

Hence, the correct statement is **'*Everybody wants to be respected by others*.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The passive voice is used to emphasize the action rather than the doer.
 
• In the passive voice, the focus is on the recipient of the action.
 
• Example:
 
 
• Active:* **"I have to do this work."***
 
• Passive: "***This work has to be done."***

questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

The meal will have been made ready by the cook by the time you reach the guest house.

options.text: The cook will have made the meal ready by the time you reach the guest house.
The cook will be making the meal ready by the time you reach the guest house.
The cook will make the meal ready by the time you reach the guest house.
The cook have made the meal ready by the time you reach the guest house.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the passive voice is used, which needs to be converted into the active voice.
 
• The subject of the passive sentence '**the cook' **becomes the **subject **of the **active sentence.**
 
• The object of the passive sentence '**the meal'** becomes the** object** of the active sentence.
 
• The verb tense "will have been made ready" is **converted** to "will have made ready" in the active voice.
 
• Format of active voice : **Subject + main verb ( here future perfect tense) + Object**

Hence, the correct active format is '***The cook will have made the meal ready by the time you reach the guest house*.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The passive voice is used to emphasize the action rather than the subject, while the** active voice** emphasizes the subject performing the action.
 
• In general, the **active voice is more direct and vigorous than the passive voice**.
 
• Converting sentences from passive to active voice often makes the sentence clearer and more concise.
 
 
• **Example: *The letter was written by John* (passive)**
 
 

 ** *John wrote the letter* (active).**

__
 
• The sentence "May you be blessed with good health" is in the** passive voice.**
 
• To convert it into the active voice, we need to identify the agent performing the action.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

It was decided by Salim Ali to devote his life to the preservation of Indian birds.

options.text: Salim Ali decided to devote his life to the preservation of Indian birds.
Salim devoted his life to the preservation of Indian birds.
Salim Ali has decided to devote his life to the preservation of Indian birds.
Salim Ali had decided to devote his life to the preservation of Indian birds.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The original sentence is in the** passive voice.**
 
• To convert it to active voice, we must identify the subject performing the action. Here, the subject is Salim Ali.
 
• The correct active form should put Salim Ali at the beginning of the sentence as the **doer **of the action.
 
• The given sentence was in past tense so the active voice here needs to maintain the **same tense. **
 
• So, it is** 'decided' ( simple past tense). **
 
• The phrase 'to devote his life to the preservation of Indian birds' remains the same in active voice 
 
• And the object **'it'** is** implicit** here.
 
 
• Format =** Subject + Verb ( simple past tense here) + Object **
 
 
 
• Option 1 transforms the sentence into the active voice without changing the meaning.

Hence, the correct active voice is '***Salim Ali decided to devote his life to the preservation of Indian birds.'***

questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

A party was organized by Rayan on his 40th Birthday.

options.text: Rayan organized a party on his 40th Birthday.
A party organized Rayan on his 40th Birthday
Rayan will be organizing a party on his 40th Birthday.
Rayan has organized a party on his 40th Birthday.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the passive voice.
 
• In the passive voice, the object of the action comes first, followed by the verb and then the subject.
 
• To convert it to the active voice, the subject comes first, followed by the verb, and then the object.
 
• Thus, "A party was organized by Rayan on his 40th Birthday." becomes "Rayan organized a party on his 40th Birthday."

Hence, the correct active voice is '***Rayan organized a party on his 40th Birthday.'***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When converting sentences from passive to active voice, ensure the subject of the active sentence is the doer of the action.
 
• Passive voice: The object + the verb "to be" + past participle + by + the subject.
 
• Active voice: The subject + the verb (in the correct tense) + the object.
 
• Example in passive voice: "The cake was eaten by the children."
 
• Example in active voice: "The children ate the cake."

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

His mother accompanies him wherever he goes.

options.text: He has accompanied his mother wherever she has gone.
He was accompanied by his mother wherever he went.
He is accompanied by his mother wherever he goes.
He accompanies his mother wherever she goes.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the active voice, and we need to convert it to the passive voice.
 
• In the passive voice, the subject of the sentence is acted upon by the verb.
 
• The structure for converting a present simple tense sentence from active to passive voice is:

 **Subject + is/am/are + past participle + by + agent**.
 
• In the given sentence, "His mother" is the subject, "accompanies" is the verb, and "him" is the object.
 
• When converting to** passive voice**, "him" becomes the subject, "is accompanied" is the verb form, and "by his mother" is the agent.

Hence, the correct passive form is : **'*He is accompanied by his mother wherever he goes*.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Passive voice is often used when the focus is on the action or when the doer of the action is unknown or unimportant.
 
• It is also used to be more formal or polite.
 
• For example: ***The book was read by the entire class.***

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Bhavna saw him carrying your suitcase.

options.text: Your suitcase carried by him was seen by Bhavna.
He was seen by Bhavna carrying your suitcase.
He had been seen by Bhavna carrying your suitcase.
Your suitcase was seen by Bhavna carrying him.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the **active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.**
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is:** "Bhavna saw him carrying your suitcase."**
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object** "him" at** the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form** "saw" to "was seen" **(simple past passive).
 
• Add the preposition** "by"** followed by the original subject **"Bhavna."**
 
• Keep the gerund phrase** "carrying your suitcase"** at the end of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** ***"He was seen by Bhavna carrying your suitcase."***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Your suitcase carried by him was seen by Bhavna." – Incorrect word order and meaning.
 
• **Option 3:** "He had been seen by Bhavna carrying your suitcase." – Incorrect tense (past perfect passive).
 
• **Option 4:** "Your suitcase was seen by Bhavna carrying him." – Incorrect meaning and structure.

questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

I am often invited by them to join their club.

options.text: I often invite them to join the club.
The club often invites me to join them.
They often invite me to join their club.
They have often invited me to join their club

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 3)**

__
 
• In the given sentence is in** passive form and** it has been changed into active voice. 

 
 
• **Object Pronoun 'them'** is changed into **subject pronoun 'they'.**
 
• Passive verb is changed into active verb and it is in simple present tense as the question is in the same tense.
 
 
 
• The verb "**invite"** is used in its base form** (V1)** and according to the subject **"they" **(3rd person plural form )
 
• The subject pronoun** 'I' **is changed into object pronoun **'me'.**
 
• The phrase **"to join their club" **is retained in the active form without any change.

Hence the correct statement is '**They often invite me to join their club.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In passive voice, the subject of the sentence **receives **the action, while in active voice, the subject **performs** the action.
 
• Passive: "I am often invited by them to join their club."
 
 
• Subject: I
 
• Verb: am invited
 
• Agent: by them
 
• Action: to join their club
 
 
 
• Active: "They often invite me to join their club."
 
 
• Subject: They
 
• Verb: invite
 
• Object: me
 
• Action: to join their club

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Pay that bill today.

options.text: That bill will be paid today.
That bill is going to be paid today.
That bill should be paid today.
Let that bill to be paid today.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an imperative sentence which is used to give orders, commands, or instructions.
 
• In passive voice, we often use the structure "**let + object + be + past participle" **for imperative sentences.
 
• However, in this case, the correct form is to use "**should be"** **to convey the necessity of the action being completed.**
 
• Therefore, the correct passive form of "Pay that bill today." is "That bill should be paid today."

Hence, the correct passive voice is '***That bill should be paid today.'***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When converting imperative sentences into passive voice, the subject of the imperative verb becomes the object of the passive verb.
 
• For example,
 
 
• **Close the door = Let the door be closed.**
 
 
 
• However, not all imperative sentences follow this format, especially when conveying necessity or obligation.
 
• **In such cases, using "should be" or "must be" is appropriate for passive constructions.**

questions.question:

options.text: The roads were repaired before the monsoon set in.
The roads had been repaired before the monsoon set in.
The roads have been repaired before the monsoon set in.

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Our rivals must have spread this rumour.

options.text: This rumour must have been spread by our rivals.
This rumour must be spread by our rivals.
This rumour may have been spread by our rivals.
This rumour has been spread by our rivals.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In converting from** active to passive** voice, the **object of the active** sentence becomes the **subject of the passive sentence.**
 
• The tense remains the same, but the form changes to fit the** passive voice structure.**
 
• The subject of the **active sentence (our rivals)** becomes the agent in the passive sentence, introduced by **'by'.**
 
• Since the **active sentence** is in perfect modal form "**must have spread**", the passive form will be "**must have been spread".**
 
• This ensures that the action is shown to have been done by someone else, specifically our rivals.

Hence, the correct statement is **'*This rumour must have been spread by our rivals.'***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Using the passive voice shifts the focus from the subject **(doer**) to the action or the object of the action.
 
• This can be useful for emphasizing the action or its recipient over the performer.
 
• In this case, the focus is on the spread of the rumour rather than who specifically spread it.

questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

Let the fire be kept burning at night.

options.text: You must burn the fire at night.
Let the fire burning at night
The fire should be burnt at night.
Keep the fire burning at night.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the original sentence, the verb is in the passive form.
 
• The active form of a sentence is where the subject performs the action stated by the verb.
 
• The given sentence "**Let the fire be kept burning at night**" implies that the fire should be actively maintained during the night.
 
• The correct active form is "**Keep the fire burning at night."**

Hence, the correct statement is '***Keep the fire burning at night*.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The passive form of a sentence typically includes a form of the verb "to be" plus the past participle of the main verb.
 
• In contrast, the active form directly states what the subject does.
 
• Understanding the distinction between active and passive forms helps in crafting clearer and more direct sentences.

__
 
• The given sentence is in the p**assive voice** and needs to be converted into the **active voice.**
 
• In the active voice, the **subject **performs the action expressed by the verb.
 
• The structure of the sentence will change from "By whom have these facts been verified?" to "Who has verified these facts?"

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

One can achieve nothing without hard work.

options.text: Nothing is achieved without hard work.
Nothing will be achieved without hard work.
Nothing has been achieved without hard work.
Nothing can be achieved without hard work.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the active voice and needs to be changed to the passive voice.
 
• In a passive voice construction, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The verb form also changes to include a form of 'to be' along with the past participle of the main verb.
 
• The correct passive construction for the given sentence is: "Nothing can be achieved without hard work."
 
• Here, "**nothing"** becomes the subject, **"can be achieved"** is the passive form of the verb, and "**without hard work**" remains the same.

Hence, the correct statement is:** *Nothing can be achieved without hard work*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In passive voice sentences, the focus is on the action rather than the subject.
 
• It is often used when the subject is unknown, unimportant, or implied.
 
• Example: "**The cake was eaten"** focuses on the action of eating rather than** who ate the cake.**
 
• Using passive voice can also make a sentence sound more formal or objective.

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Grow more trees.

options.text: Let more trees be grown.
You should grow more trees.
More trees should be growing.
More trees should grow.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passive form of an imperative sentence is constructed using the phrase 'let' followed by the object and the past participle of the verb.
 
• In this case, the original sentence is 'Grow more trees.' Here, **'more trees**' is the object, and **'grown**' is the past participle of '**grow'**.
 
• Therefore, the correct passive form is 'Let more trees be grown.' 
 
• Format of imperative voice change = **Let + Subject + be + V3 + Object (if any)**

Hence, the correct passive form is **'*Let more trees be grown.'***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Imperative sentences are **commands, requests, or instructions.**
 
• In the passive voice, the focus is shifted from the **subject to the action itself.**
 
• Passive voice is often used to make the sentence sound more **formal** or to emphasize the action rather than the subject.
